decisions.reason: This is essentially a rebranded version of an already accepted machine with visible website promotion and stated prior market acceptance, so dropping it would force an unnecessary write-off of an established commitment.

As a publicly presented product line with several models, it likely involved meaningful engineering and marketing investment, which management would be reluctant to reverse after only a short time on the market.

Although it was only mentioned rather than heavily promoted, it is still a multi-model line in a strategic mobile processing segment, so early weak results can still be framed as a temporary market ramp-up issue.

This single stationary electric fine shredder has the weakest visible commitment among the launches, but because it fits the firm's stationary recycling direction and is still very new, management is likely to give it more time rather than admit failure quickly.

Despite limited website prominence, this multi-model green-waste grinder line reflects nontrivial investment and aligns with resource-saving recycling markets, making continuation more likely than withdrawal.
A separately presented product line with several models signals strong public and resource commitment, so escalation of commitment makes a near-term withdrawal unlikely.
